column2: relocation-key ambiguity on either the old baseline side or the live findings side must raise `baselineerror` before any `--initial-reason` fallback runs. without explicit per-side relocation-key counts and an ambiguity hard-stop, duplicate old rows sharing one relocation key (e.g. stale flat path plus new package path during partial regen) can last-win a reason or silently assign one bootstrap reason to a collision instead of failing closed.

plan and test bullets allow satisfying ambiguity coverage with only one collision shape (or-combined old-row collision or live-finding collision). edge cases require failing when two old rows explain one live finding and when one old row explains two live findings; exercising only one direction leaves the opposite regression undetected.

the env move-preservation plan never requires a write run without `--initial-reason` on the relocated fixture. that leaves the unmatched-new-env contract unverified on the new package path; a default-reason regression could ship while tests still pass.

the env relocation key uses only basename, env_name, constant, and access, unlike the subprocess linter which also includes qualified_symbol and occurrence. after a flat-to-package move, `larch/agents/agents.py` already baselines many distinct `implement_tmpdir` get rows across different qualified_symbols; both baseline and live sides would collapse into one relocation key with counts well above 1, so `--write` would raise `baselineerror` and still require manual `--initial-reason`, leaving the packaging-move failure mode unfixed for the env ratchet.

the prior-round env relocation write test is still not named in the plan. the env test section has orphan bullets describing flat baseline to `larch/agents/...` preservation but no `test_write_preserves_reason_after_package_move_without_initial_reason` entry mirroring subprocess; only `test_write_fails_on_unmatched_env_finding_without_initial_reason` is listed, so a default-reason regression on relocated package paths could ship with passing tests.

the plan's `python/lint_env_via_config_constant.py` relocation-key bullets list only `env_name`, `constant`, and `access`. that contradicts the plan's own edge-case prose and the subprocess mirror, which require basename plus full semantic identity (`path(file).name`, `qualified_symbol`, `occurrence`). real `larch/agents/agents.py` baselines already contain many distinct `implement_tmpdir` `get` rows that share the same env tuple across different `qualified_symbol` values and occurrences. a three-field key collapses those rows, per-side relocation counts exceed 1, `--write` raises `baselineerror` instead of preserving reasons after a package move, and the env packaging-move ratchet stays broken.
